Consider the polar curve $r=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +2,$ shown above. Given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta +a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{3\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }
$$

find the value of $a-b.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14065566/assets/5bbb314322763dad82b0390e9d9713ab551de16208a2eb0b75c4ceb3c1f9c611.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the polar curve $r=-5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use the formula for differentiating parametric curves:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}
$$

First, we recall that to convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Using the fact that $r=-5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =-5{cos}^{2}⁡\theta , \\ y & =-5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta =-\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ,\end{aligned}
$$

where we used the identity $\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

To compute our derivative, we first need to calculate ${x}^{′}(\theta )$ and ${y}^{′}(\theta ):$ 

- First, we compute the derivative of $x$ with respect to $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\theta ) & =(-5{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )^{′} \\  & =-10\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\  & =10\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta \end{aligned}
$$

- Then, we compute the derivative of $y$ with respect to $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\theta ) & ={(-\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta )}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta \cdot 2) \\  & =-5\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )} \\  & =\frac{-5\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{5\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta } \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡2\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
